thread:
Emily Tran: Opened a small consolidation PR for Dedicated docs: migration checklist (reserved -> dedicated), an autoscale FAQ snippet, and a compact SDK example for tenant labeling. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4578. Please check the SLA phrasing and the eviction note.

Raj Patel: Quick read. Avoid using 'best-effort' alone; suggest: 'Dedicated capacity has SLA-backed targets; burst/shared fallback tiers are not SLA-backed and can be preempted.' Also add a short sentence about scheduled maintenance causing temporary preemptions.

Sam Kim: YAML snippet suggestion: include explicit tenant labels so it's obvious to users. Example: `labels:\n  tenant_label: "team-omega"\n  isolation: "tenant"` under allocation.

Claire Jones: Found a stale handbook anchor in the migration checklist. Replace `#reserved-vs-dedicated` with `#capacity-modes`. I can push the tiny fix if you want.

Marc Brown: SDK snippet for the "Programmatic provisioning" section: 

```python
import os
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
cap = client.create_capacity(
    name="team-omega-dedicated",
    region="us-west-2",
    scale_policy={"min_replicas": 2, "max_replicas": 8, "cooldown_seconds": 300, "policy": "throughput_based"},
    labels={"tenant_label": "team-omega", "isolation": "tenant"}
)
print(cap)
```

Marc Brown: Add a short inline note: runtime may still preempt for infra maintenance; surface in SLA section.

Liz Yang: Recommend bumping default cooldown to 300s (60s tends to oscillate in simulations). Also add a brief test plan in the doc: 1) spike -> verify scale up, 2) sustained load -> verify stability, 3) cooldown -> verify scale down delayed, 4) eviction -> verify fallback behavior.

docs-bot: Lint: docs/lint passed. Link check: 1 broken anchor fixed (thanks @Claire Jones).

Emily Tran: Thanks everyone. I'll apply Claire's anchor change, add Marc's SDK snippet, set cooldown to 300, and add Raj's SLA wording for legal review: "Dedicated capacity is covered by SLA-backed latency targets; fallback tiers (burst/shared) are not SLA-backed and may be preempted for maintenance or capacity constraints." I'll also add the test plan and a final checklist item to verify tenant labels after cutover. If no objections I'll merge after CI. :thumbsup:

Raj Patel: :thumbsup:

Sam Kim: lgtm

Claire Jones: Pushed the anchor fix as a small commit.

Marc Brown: Follow-up: let's also add a debug step in the migration checklist for checking label propagation in the console.

Emily Tran: Good idea, adding that as the penultimate step. Merging after CI green and legal thumbs.
